visible.name: Aguinid Falls
visible.address: Barangay Tangbo, Samboan, Cebu
visible.description: Hindi lang titingnan, aakyatin mo! Aguinid Falls in Tangbo, Samboan has five tiers along the Tangbo River, and each level has its own waterfall. With a local guide, you climb the smooth limestone walls between tiers, swim in turquoise basins and slide down where it's safe. It's an adventurous, less crowded alternative
visible.best_time_to_visit: Mornings in the dry season
visible.commute_access: Ceres bus toward Bato/Samboan from Cebu South Bus Terminal (about 3.5-4 hours) or around 20-30 minutes from Oslob.
visible.budget_note: Entrance fee plus a required local guide.

visible.name: Aling Lucing's Sisig
visible.address: Glaciano Valdez Street (near the old railway 'Crossing'), Angeles City, Pampanga
visible.description: Ito ang lugar kung saan nagsimula ang sizzling sisig! In 1974, Lucia "Aling Lucing" Cunanan grilled and chopped pig ears and cheeks, seasoned them with vinegar, calamansi, onions and chicken liver, and served it all on a hot plate beside the railway in Angeles. That dish helped make Angeles the "Sisig Capital of the Ph
visible.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon to late night
visible.commute_access: From Manila, take a bus to Angeles/Dau terminal (around 1.5–2 hours via NLEX), then a jeep or tricycle to the Crossing area.
visible.budget_note: Sisig plates are budget-friendly (Wikivoyage notes up to around ₱199 at a branch).

visible.name: Alona Beach
visible.address: Barangay Tawala, Panglao, Bohol
visible.description: Powdery white sand, clear water, and a full strip of restaurants, dive shops and bars – Alona Beach is the easy, buhay na buhay base of most Bohol trips. visible.best_time_to_visit: November to May; sunset for dinner
visible.commute_access: About 15 minutes from Bohol-Panglao International Airport; around 30 minutes from Tagbilaran port by car or tricycle.
visible.budget_note: Beach is free; food from budget to mid-range.

visible.name: Anawangin Cove
visible.address: Anawangin Cove, San Antonio, Zambales
visible.description: Camp under 'pine' trees by the sea – Anawangin Cove looks like nowhere else in the country. This crescent cove has grayish-white sand backed by a grove of agoho trees and grassy mountains, a landscape shaped by Mt. Pinatubo's ash. A boat ride from Pundaquit gets you there, and most barkadas stay overnight: pitch a tent

visible.commute_access: From Manila, take a Victory Liner bus to San Antonio/Iba, Zambales (around 4–5 hours), then a tricycle to Brgy. Pundaquit and a boat to Anawangin (around 30 min

visible.name: Angono–Binangonan Petroglyphs
visible.address: Eastridge Avenue, Binangonan, Rizal
visible.description: See the oldest known artwork in the Philippines up close. The Angono-Binangonan Petroglyphs are 127 figures carved into a rock shelter wall, believed to date from the Late Neolithic, before 2000 BC. National Artist Carlos 'Botong' Francisco reported them in 1965, and today the National Museum runs a site museum plus a
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings, Tuesday to Sunday
visible.commute_access: From Metro Manila, ride to Angono or Binangonan via Ortigas Extension/Manila East Road, then a tricycle up to the Eastridge site (around 1–1.5 hours total).
visible.budget_note: Around PHP 200 entrance.

visible.name: Anilao (Diving and Snorkeling)
visible.address: Anilao, Mabini, Batangas
visible.description: Ang 'birthplace of Philippine scuba diving' - and still one of the world's best macro dive spots, just about 2.5 hours from Manila. Anilao, in Mabini, Batangas, faces Balayan Bay at the edge of the Verde Island Passage, often called the center of the center of marine shorefish biodiversity. Divers come for nudibranchs,
visible.best_time_to_visit: Around Nov-May for calmer seas; Mar-May is peak season, so book early
visible.commute_access: From Manila, take a bus to Batangas City Grand Terminal (around 2–3 hours via STAR Tollway), then a jeep to Mabini/Anilao port and a tricycle to your resort. Mo

visible.name: Apo Island
visible.address: Apo Island, Dauin, Negros Oriental
visible.description: Swimming with pawikan! Apo Island is a small volcanic island off southern Negros and one of the world's most famous community-run marine sanctuaries. In 1982, Dr. Angel Alcala of Silliman University convinced local fishers to protect their reef, and it paid off: over 650 fish species and around 400 coral species live h
visible.best_time_to_visit: Calm-sea months, March to June; mornings
visible.commute_access: From Dumaguete, jeep or van about 30 minutes to Malatapay, then boat about 30-45 minutes to Apo Island. Dauin dive resorts also run trips.
visible.budget_note: Boat rental (shared or private), marine sanctuary and snorkeling fees, plus guide.

visible.name: Ariel's Point
visible.address: Buruanga, Aklan (boat trip from Boracay)
visible.description: Talon ka ba? Ariel's Point is Boracay's favorite adventure day trip, a rocky cove on the Buruanga coast with cliff-diving platforms at 5, 8 and 15 metres. A boat leaves from Station 1, and once there you can jump, kayak, paddleboard, snorkel or hike the nature trail. Not into jumping? Cheering from the deck counts too.
visible.best_time_to_visit: November to May for calm seas
visible.commute_access: Book a package from Boracay; the boat departs from Station 1 area or the operator's meeting point.
visible.budget_note: Day packages typically run around PHP 3,000 and up, often with lunch and drinks.

visible.name: Art in Island
visible.address: 175 15th Ave, Brgy. Socorro, Cubao, Quezon City, 1109 Metro Manila
visible.description: Dito, bawal ang 'do not touch' - you are part of the art! visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday afternoons for shorter photo queues; any rainy day
visible.commute_access: Commute-friendly via MRT-3 Araneta Center-Cubao or LRT-2 Cubao, then short ride or walk depending on route.
visible.budget_note: Plan around PHP 850 per person for admission or the basic visit. Special exhibits, guided activities, workshops, and transport may cost extra.

visible.name: Baguio City Public Market
visible.address: Magsaysay Avenue, Baguio City
visible.description: Gusto mo ng real Baguio? Dito ka sa palengke. The Baguio City Public Market is a sprawling, busy maze where locals shop for highland vegetables, fresh strawberries, cut flowers, longganisa and Benguet coffee, plus woven fabrics, beads and wood carvings from around the Cordillera. visible.address: Harrison Road, Baguio City

visible.name: Balicasag Island (and Pamilacan Dolphin Watching)
visible.address: Balicasag Island, Panglao, Bohol
visible.description: The highlight of any Panglao island hopping trip. Boats leave around dawn to look for dolphins near Pamilacan, then head to Balicasag, a marine sanctuary about 8 km off Alona Beach and Bohol's most famous dive spot. visible.best_time_to_visit: March to May; leave around 6am for dolphins
visible.commute_access: Boats depart from Alona Beach or Panglao resorts, about 30-45 minutes to Balicasag.
visible.budget_note: Shared tours around PHP 1,000-1,800; private boats per group; snorkel fees paid on the island.

visible.name: Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park

visible.name: Baluarte de San Diego

visible.name: Bangui Windmills
visible.address: Bangui Bay, Bangui, Ilocos Norte
visible.description: Ang iconic Ilocos photo! Twenty giant wind turbines stand in a single row along about 9 km of Bangui Bay's shore, each 70 meters tall with 41-meter blades turning slowly above the dark sand. visible.budget_note: Free.

visible.name: Barasoain Church
visible.address: Paseo del Congreso, Malolos City, Bulacan
visible.description: This is where the Philippines first became a republic. Barasoain Church in Malolos, completed in 1888, hosted the Malolos Congress from September 15, 1898, and the inauguration of the First Philippine Republic on January 23, 1899, with Emilio Aguinaldo sworn in as president. visible.name: Barracuda Lake

visible.name: Basco Lighthouse (Naidi Hills)

visible.name: Basilica Minore del Santo Niño

visible.name: Batad Rice Terraces
visible.address: Barangay Batad, Banaue, Ifugao
visible.description: Ito ang terraces na parang amphitheater ng mga diyos. Founded in 2009 by National Artist Benedicto 'BenCab' Cabrera, this four-storey museum on Asin Road is easily one of the best art spaces in the country. visible.budget_note: Around ₱200 general admission, with student/senior discounts. Café meals extra.

visible.name: Biak-na-Bato National Park
visible.address: Brgy. Biak-na-Bato, San Miguel / Doña Remedios Trinidad, Bulacan
visible.description: History lesson plus nature trip in one! visible.commute_access: From Manila, take a bus to San Miguel, Bulacan (around 2 hours via NLEX/Baliuag), then a tricycle to the park entrance (around 30 minutes).
visible.budget_note: Entrance and guide fees.

visible.name: Bilar Man-Made Forest

visible.best_time_to_visit: Morning or late afternoon, in daylight
visible.commute_access: On the main road between Loboc and Bilar, about 1 hour from Tagbilaran.

visible.commute_access: Register in town, then take a jeep/van to the Banga-an jump-off (about 20–30 minutes) and trek with a guide.
visible.budget_note: Guide fee per group plus shared transport; environmental fee separate.

visible.name: Boracay Sunset Paraw Sailing
visible.address: White Beach (boarding points along Stations 1-3), Boracay Island, Malay, Aklan
visible.description: Ang pinaka-Boracay na gawin pag golden hour! Hop on a paraw, a traditional Filipino double-outrigger sailboat, and sit on the netting while it glides along White Beach as the sky turns orange and pink. With a crab-claw sail and nothing but wind, it's quiet, breezy and very photogenic. Rides usually last 30 minutes to a
visible.best_time_to_visit: Around 5 PM to sunset, November to May
visible.commute_access: Book directly with boatmen on White Beach or through apps like Klook.
visible.budget_note: Prices are per boat or per person and rise at sunset; around PHP 2,500-4,000 per boat is common, so split with friends.

visible.name: Britania Group of Islands
visible.address: Barangay Britania, San Agustin, Surigao del Sur
visible.description: Mindanao's island-hopping gem! Britania is a group of 24 islets with white sandbars scattered across Lianga Bay off San Agustin, Surigao del Sur, facing the Philippine Sea. Hop to Hiyor-Hiyoran with its palm-lined white beach, then Boslon for turquoise water framed by rocky cliffs, with plenty of stops for swimming and
visible.best_time_to_visit: March to September when the sea is calmer
visible.commute_access: Ride a bus from Butuan, Tandag or Bislig to San Agustin, then a tricycle to Barangay Britania where boats depart. It is about 2 hours by road from Hinatuan.
visible.budget_note: Boats are hired per group at the Britania boat landing in San Agustin, so the cost drops when you split it with your barkada. Bring cash, food and water.

visible.name: Bulabog Beach (Kitesurfing)
visible.address: East coast, Balabag, Boracay Island, Malay, Aklan
visible.description: Kites, sails, and non-stop wind – Bulabog is Boracay's other beach, and during Amihan season it turns into one of Asia's best spots for kitesurfing and windsurfing. Hills at both ends of the island funnel the northeast wind straight onshore, so the bay fills with colorful kites. Watch the action from the sand with a dr
visible.best_time_to_visit: November to March for steady Amihan winds
visible.visit_duration: 1-2 hours to watch; lessons run several days
visible.commute_access: About 5-10 minutes walk across the island from Station 2 via D'Mall area.
visible.budget_note: Free to watch; kitesurfing lessons are pricey (several thousand pesos per session).

visible.name: Burnham Park
visible.address: Jose Abad Santos Drive, Baguio City, Benguet
visible.description: Baguio's green heart just got a glow-up. Burnham Park, the 32-hectare park named after American architect Daniel Burnham, who drew up the city's plan in 1905, is the easiest pine-shaded break downtown. Its lake reopened on September 1, 2026, after a ₱100-million rehabilitation, with boating back in action - so rent a s
visible.best_time_to_visit: Early weekday mornings (6-9am); expect crowds on Panagbenga weekends
visible.commute_access: From Manila, take a Victory Liner, Genesis/Joy Bus or Solid North bus to Baguio (around 4–6 hours via TPLEX). From the Gov. Pack Road or Harrison Road terminals
visible.budget_note: Free entry. Boat and bike rentals cost extra (roughly ₱100–₱250 per 30 mins–1 hour).

visible.name: Café by the Ruins
visible.address: 25 Shuntug Street, Baguio City
visible.description: Ang breakfast na hinahanap-hanap ng Baguio regulars. Café by the Ruins opened in 1988, started by a group of Baguio artists and writers including National Artist BenCab, and it is built among the ruins of a structure destroyed in World War II. The result: a leafy, open dining room with stone walls, plants and local art
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday breakfast; come early on weekends to beat the line
visible.commute_access: Walkable from Burnham Park and City Hall area, about 10 minutes from Session Road.
visible.budget_note: Mains around ₱300–₱600; plan around ₱400–₱800 per person.

visible.name: Cagayan de Oro White Water Rafting
visible.address: Cagayan de Oro River (jump-off around Barangay Mambuaya), Cagayan de Oro City, Misamis Oriental
visible.description: Paddle hard, scream louder! White water rafting on the Cagayan de Oro River is the city's banner tourism activity, and it's the ultimate barkada adrenaline day in Northern Mindanao. Outfitters take you from the jump-off in Barangay Mambuaya, about 30-40 minutes from the city, down a run of rapids between gorges and gre
visible.best_time_to_visit: Mornings; year-round for beginner runs
visible.commute_access: From Laguindingan Airport, about 1 hour to CDO city; rafting outfitters pick up from city hotels to the jump-off (about 30-45 minutes).
visible.budget_note: Beginner packages commonly start around PHP 1,200; advanced runs cost more. Use DOT-accredited operators.

visible.name: Cagsawa Ruins and Mayon ATV Tours
visible.address: Brgy. Busay, Daraga, Albay
visible.description: Ang pinaka-iconic na view sa Bicol! The lone belfry of Cagsawa Church stands in a park with the near-perfect cone of Mayon Volcano rising behind it. The Franciscan church was rebuilt in 1724, then destroyed with the whole town of Cagsawa in Mayon's eruption on February 1, 1814. Today the ruins are protected by Daraga a
visible.best_time_to_visit: Early morning (6-8 AM); drier months around March to May
visible.commute_access: Fly Manila–Daraga (Bicol International Airport, about 1 hour) or take an overnight bus to Legazpi (around 10–12 hours). From Legazpi, ride a jeep to Daraga and
visible.budget_note: Small entrance fee to the park; ATV rides priced by route and duration (from around a thousand pesos up).

visible.name: Calauit Safari Park
visible.address: Calauit Island, Busuanga, Palawan
visible.description: Safari sa Palawan, totoo! Calauit Safari Park on Calauit Island in northern Busuanga is where reticulated giraffes and Grevy's zebras roam free, descendants of African animals brought here in 1976. Rangers take you around the island, and on many tours you get to hand-feed the giraffes. The park also protects Philippine
visible.best_time_to_visit: Dry season (November to May); morning for feeding
visible.commute_access: From Coron town, about 2-3 hours by van to Buluang port, then a short boat crossing to Calauit; most go via a tour with hotel pickup.
visible.budget_note: Shared day tours with transport, entrance and lunch typically cost a few thousand pesos.

visible.name: Calea Pastries and Coffee
visible.address: Lacson Street, Bacolod City, Negros Occidental
visible.description: Sweet tooth ka? Calea is the cake stop almost every Bacolod trip includes, and the line at night proves it. The draw is simple: big, generous slices that taste premium but stay friendly to the wallet. Barkadas pile a table with chocolate cake, white chocolate cheesecake with raspberry and pecan pie, then pass the forks
visible.best_time_to_visit: Mid-afternoon merienda, or after dinner if you do not mind a short line
visible.commute_access: Along Lacson Street; about 10 minutes by jeep or taxi from downtown Bacolod.
visible.budget_note: Cake slices are affordable, roughly PHP 100-200.

visible.name: Callao Cave
visible.address: Barangay Magdalo / Quibal, Peñablanca, Cagayan
visible.description: Callao Cave is Cagayan's best-known natural attraction and a real history spot. Climb 184 concrete steps to the entrance, then walk through seven limestone chambers. The biggest chamber is a natural chapel, with a rock altar lit by sunlight streaming through holes in the roof. In 2007, scientists found fossils here lat
visible.best_time_to_visit: Morning, when sunlight enters the chapel chamber; dry season (December–May)
visible.commute_access: About 24 km northeast of Tuguegarao City. Tuguegarao is a 1-hour flight or about 12-hour bus ride (around ₱600) from Manila; from the city, hire a van or tricyc
visible.budget_note: Hard hats are required inside and rent for ₱20 each. Bring extra cash for the entrance, the river crossing, the Pinacanauan boat ride and guide tips.

visible.name: Calle Crisologo
visible.address: Calle Crisologo, Vigan City, Ilocos Sur
visible.description: Parang time travel! Calle Crisologo is the cobblestone heart of Vigan, the best-preserved Spanish colonial town in Asia according to UNESCO. Both sides of the street are lined with old bahay na bato houses with capiz windows, heavy wooden floors and balconies, many now turned into antique shops, cafés and souvenir stor
visible.best_time_to_visit: Early morning for empty-street photos; evening for the lamplit look; Nov-May dry season
visible.commute_access: From Manila (Cubao/Sampaloc/Pasay), take a Partas, Dominion or Florida bus to Vigan (around 8–10 hours). Calle Crisologo is a short tricycle ride or walk from t
visible.budget_note: Free to walk. Kalesa tours are priced per hour or per route (agree before riding).

visible.name: Cambugahay Falls
visible.address: Barangay Campalanas, Lazi, Siquijor
visible.description: Siquijor's star attraction: three tiers of turquoise pools flowing through the jungle in Lazi. Swing from the famous rope swing, ride a bamboo raft, or just soak in the cool, spring-fed water with the barkada. You'll walk down a long flight of concrete steps from the road, and a local guide fee is usually collected at
visible.best_time_to_visit: Early morning; dry season for the clearest water
visible.commute_access: Ferry from Dumaguete to Siquijor or Larena port (about 1-1.5 hours), then about 45 minutes by scooter or tricycle to Lazi.
visible.budget_note: Environmental or guide fee, plus rope swing tips.

visible.name: Camp John Hay
visible.address: Loakan Road, Camp John Hay, Baguio City
visible.description: Pine trees, cool air and a lot of history - Camp John Hay is Baguio's leafiest hangout. It started in the early 1900s as an American hill station and military reservation, and today it is a forest watershed and tourist area run by the BCDA. Walk the shaded Yellow Trail under the pines, then head to the Historical Core
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings for the trails; Nov-Apr for dry, cool weather
visible.commute_access: Take a jeepney bound for Camp John Hay/Scout Barrio from downtown or a taxi (around 10–15 minutes from Session Road).
visible.budget_note: Yellow Trail is free. Historical Core around ₱85 adult; Tree Top Adventure rides priced separately.

visible.name: Campuestohan Highland Resort
visible.address: Barangay Cabatangan, Talisay City, Negros Occidental
visible.description: Larger than life, literally! Campuestohan Highland Resort in the cool hills of Talisay City, Negros Occidental is the kitschy theme-park resort famous for its giant King Kong, dinosaurs and its Guinness-record chicken-shaped hotel. Spend the day riding the zipline across the resort, splashing in the pools and wave pool
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings for clear views; December for the Christmas village
visible.commute_access: About 1 hour by private car or tour from Bacolod; Klook offers day tours with transfers.
visible.budget_note: Entrance fee plus paid rides.

visible.name: CamSur Watersports Complex (CWC)
visible.address: Provincial Capitol Complex, Cadlan, Pili, Camarines Sur
visible.description: Tara, wakeboarding sa Bicol! The CamSur Watersports Complex (CWC) in Pili, about 20 minutes from Naga City, has been called the mecca of water sports parks in the Philippines since it opened in 2006. Beginners start with kneeboarding on the beginner cable while pros hit the ramps and sliders on the main lake, and there
visible.best_time_to_visit: Dry season mornings or late afternoons; weekdays for shorter waits
visible.commute_access: Fly Manila–Naga (Pili airport, around 1 hour) or take an overnight bus to Naga (around 8–10 hours). CWC is around 15–20 minutes from Naga City by jeep, van or t
visible.budget_note: Cable time is sold by the hour or day, plus gear rental.

visible.name: Cape Bojeador Lighthouse
visible.address: Vigia de Nagparitan Hill, Burgos, Ilocos Norte
visible.description: Over 130 years and still shining! Cape Bojeador Lighthouse was first lit on March 30, 1892, and still guides ships from Vigia de Nagpartian Hill in Burgos, marking the northwesternmost point of Luzon. Climb the brick steps up the hill, admire the 20-meter octagonal stone tower and the old red-brick keeper's buildings,
visible.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon; dry season (November to May)
visible.commute_access: About 1 hour north of Laoag by car or Pagudpud-bound bus; get off at Burgos and take a tricycle up the hill.
visible.budget_note: Donations accepted.

visible.name: Capones Island Lighthouse
visible.address: Capones Island, Pundaquit, San Antonio, Zambales
visible.description: A Spanish-era lighthouse on a wild, rocky island – the best view on any Zambales island-hopping trip. Capones Island sits about 3.8 km off Pundaquit, all steep cliffs and rock formations ringed by white sand and coral. Boats drop you on the beach, then a short, steep trail climbs to the Faro de Punta Capones, a brick t
visible.best_time_to_visit: Calm-sea mornings, November to May
visible.commute_access: Boat from Pundaquit, San Antonio (around 20–30 minutes), usually bundled with Anawangin or Nagsasa trips.
visible.budget_note: Island-hopping boat rental per group plus small fees.

visible.name: Caramoan Island Hopping (Matukad, Lahos, Sabitang Laya)
visible.address: Caramoan Peninsula, Caramoan, Camarines Sur (boats from Paniman/Gota)
visible.description: Survivor-level ganda! Caramoan in Camarines Sur is all dramatic limestone islets, powdery white-sand coves and clear water, so wild that more than a dozen international editions of Survivor were filmed here. A day of island hopping from Paniman usually covers Matukad with its hidden lagoon, Lahos and its sandbar, and S
visible.best_time_to_visit: March to June for calmer seas
visible.commute_access: Fly or bus to Naga, then a van to Sabang Port in San José and a boat to Guijalo Port, Caramoan (around 2 hours), then a tricycle to Paniman for island-hopping b
visible.budget_note: Island-hopping boats are rented per group; plus environmental fees and transfers.

visible.name: Casa Gorordo Museum
visible.address: 35 Lopez Jaena Street, Parian, Cebu City, Cebu
visible.description: Silipin ang buhay ng mayamang pamilyang Cebuano noong 1800s! Casa Gorordo is an 1850s house in Parian that was home to four generations of the Gorordo family, including Juan Gorordo, the first Filipino bishop of Cebu. The Ramon Aboitiz Foundation bought and restored it, and it opened in 1983 as Cebu's first public muse
visible.best_time_to_visit: Tuesday to Sunday mornings; great on a rainy day
visible.commute_access: Short taxi or Grab ride from downtown Cebu.
visible.budget_note: Entrance fee applies; students and seniors may get discounts.

visible.name: Casa Manila
visible.address: Plaza San Luis Complex, General Luna corner Real Streets, Intramuros, Manila
visible.description: Ever wondered how a rich family lived in 1800s Manila? Casa Manila in Plaza San Luis, right across San Agustin Church, shows you room by room. This three-story bahay na bato was built in the 1980s as a replica of an 1850s house that once stood on Calle Jaboneros in San Nicolas, and it is filled with period furniture, a
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; closed Mondays
visible.commute_access: Walkable from Manila Cathedral and San Agustin Church; reachable from LRT-1 Central Terminal via jeep, e-trike, or taxi.
visible.budget_note: Plan around PHP 75 per person for admission or the basic visit. Special exhibits, guided activities, workshops, and transport may cost extra.

visible.name: Casaroro Falls

Getting there is half the adventure: a long staircase down, then boulder-hopping along the river, which keeps the crowds small. Your reward is a cool dip
visible.best_time_to_visit: Mornings in the dry season
visible.commute_access: About 30-45 minutes from Dumaguete via Valencia by habal-habal or private car.
visible.budget_note: Small entrance fee.

visible.name: Cebu Taoist Temple
visible.address: Beverly Hills Subdivision, Lahug, Cebu City, Cebu
visible.description: A red-and-gold temple on a hill with one of the best views of Cebu City. Built in 1972 by Cebu's Chinese-Filipino community, the Cebu Taoist Temple sits in Beverly Hills, Lahug, about 110 m above sea level. Enter through a mini Great Wall of China, then climb past dragon-topped roofs to the viewing areas over the city.
visible.best_time_to_visit: Morning or late afternoon
visible.commute_access: About 15-20 minutes by taxi or Grab from Cebu IT Park or Ayala Center.
visible.budget_note: Free entry; donations welcome.

visible.name: Celera
visible.address: 3F, Comuna, 238 Pablo Ocampo Sr. Extension, Makati
visible.description: Dark, moody and full of umami – Celera is a one-Michelin-star dining room on the 3rd floor of Comuna, run by chef-owners Nicco Santos and Quenee Vilar. They call their food 'marriage cuisine': contemporary Asian cooking that blends Japanese, Chinese, Singaporean and other influences, built on dashi, fermentation and a
visible.best_time_to_visit: Dinner, booked in advance
visible.commute_access: Best reached by car or ride-hailing; it sits off Pablo Ocampo Sr. Extension near the Makati-Manila boundary.
visible.budget_note: Top-tier Michelin pricing, around ₱5,000 and up per person.

visible.name: Chocolate Hills Complex
visible.address: Chocolate Hills Complex, Barangay Buenos Aires, Carmen, Bohol
visible.description: Bohol's most famous view, at kailangang makita in person! At least 1,260 cone-shaped limestone hills, possibly over 1,700, roll across more than 50 square kilometers of the Bohol countryside. In the dry season the grass turns cocoa-brown, which gave them their name; in the rainy months they're lush green. Climb the sta
visible.best_time_to_visit: Early morning or late afternoon; around February to May for the brown 'chocolate' look
visible.commute_access: About 1.5-2 hours by car or bus from Tagbilaran or Panglao (Bohol-Panglao International Airport); countryside tours include it.
visible.budget_note: Environmental/entrance fee around PHP 100.

visible.name: Cloud 9 Boardwalk
visible.address: Tourism Road, Barangay Catangnan, General Luna, Siargao, Surigao del Norte
visible.description: The wave that made Siargao famous - and in 2026 it joins the world's top surf tour. Cloud 9 is a hollow right-hand reef break off General Luna, the reason the town is called the 'Surfing Capital of the Philippines'. A wooden boardwalk runs over the reef to a viewing platform where you can watch surfers drop into the ba
visible.best_time_to_visit: August to November for surf season; sunrise or sunset for the boardwalk
visible.commute_access: From Sayak Airport (Del Carmen), about 45 minutes to 1 hour by van to General Luna; from Dapa port, about 30 minutes by tricycle or habal-habal.
visible.budget_note: Free to visit the boardwalk; surf lessons and board rentals extra.

visible.name: Coconut Road and Sea of Palms Viewpoint
visible.address: Circumferential Road, between General Luna and Pilar, Siargao, Surigao del Norte
visible.description: Endless coconut palms as far as you can see - this is the Siargao view on every postcard. The circumferential road out of General Luna winds through a sea of palms, and the elevated viewpoint lets you look over the canopy rolling to the hills. Come at sunrise, when mist hangs over the trees and the light turns everythi
visible.best_time_to_visit: Sunrise
visible.commute_access: About 30 minutes by scooter from General Luna along the circumferential road.
visible.budget_note: Free; some viewpoints ask a small fee.

visible.name: Cuatro Islas
visible.address: Digyo Island, Inopacan, Leyte
visible.description: Four islands, one epic island-hopping day! Cuatro Islas is a protected landscape and seascape off western Leyte: Digyo, Apid and Mahaba belong to Inopacan, while Himokilan belongs to Hindang. Digyo is the crowd favorite, with white sand, turquoise water and coral reefs for snorkeling. Apid has a photogenic floating hut
visible.best_time_to_visit: March to June for calm seas
visible.commute_access: Ride a bus or van from Ormoc or Tacloban to Inopacan, then hire a pumpboat at the Inopacan shore to the islands.
visible.budget_note: Pumpboats to the islands are chartered per boat at Inopacan, so the cost drops when you split it with your barkada. Bring cash and pack your own food and water.

visible.name: Cubao Expo
visible.address: 3 General Romulo Ave, Cubao, Quezon City, 1109 Metro Manila
visible.description: Vintage finds by day, beer and gigs by night - Cubao Expo is QC's creative hideout. Built in the 1970s as the Marikina Shoe Expo, a hub for locally made shoes, this compact compound in Araneta City later filled up with antique and vintage shops, record stores, galleries, cafes, bars and restaurants. Today it is a favor
visible.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon into the evening; weekends for the liveliest crowd
visible.commute_access: Very commute-friendly via MRT-3 Araneta Center-Cubao or LRT-2 Cubao, then short walk through the Cubao area.
visible.budget_note: Plan around PHP 200 per person as a starting activity budget. Rentals, equipment, add-ons, booking fees, food, and premium packages may raise the total.

visible.commute_access: About 1.5 hours by car from Cagayan de Oro via Manolo Fortich; or bus to Manolo Fortich then habal-habal up.
visible.budget_note: Small entrance fee plus per-ride prices; the dual zipline and Dropzone are the pricier ones.

visible.name: Danao Adventure Park (EAT Danao)
visible.address: Barangay Magtangtang, Danao, Bohol
visible.description: Ready to scream with the barkada? Danao Adventure Park, better known as EAT Danao, is Bohol's extreme playground, set on a 144-hectare spread of gorges, river and forest. The headline ride is The Plunge, a canyon swing that drops you over the Wahig River gorge, but there's plenty more: ziplines, the sky ride, river kay
visible.best_time_to_visit: Dry season mornings
visible.visit_duration: Half day (plus about 2 hours' drive each way from Panglao)
visible.commute_access: About 2-2.5 hours by car from Tagbilaran or Panglao.
visible.budget_note: Activities priced individually; The Plunge is one of the pricier rides.

visible.name: Daraga Church
visible.address: Santa Maria Hill, Daraga, Albay
visible.description: Simbahan na may front-row view ng Mayon! Daraga Church, officially the Church of Nuestra Señora de la Porteria, was built by the Franciscans in 1773 on a hilltop in Daraga, overlooking both the sea and Mayon Volcano. Its Churrigueresque Baroque facade of volcanic stone is covered in intricate carvings, and parts of the
visible.best_time_to_visit: Early morning for clear Mayon views; drier months around March to May
visible.commute_access: From Legazpi, ride a jeep to Daraga town (around 15 minutes), then walk or tricycle up the hill.
visible.budget_note: Free; respect mass schedules.

visible.name: Daranak Falls
visible.address: Brgy. Tandang Kutyo, Tanay, Rizal
visible.description: Tara, langoy sa malamig na tubig ng Rizal! Daranak Falls is a 14-metre curtain of water dropping into a wide, cool basin, just a short walk from the road in Tanay. It's one of the most popular nature spots in Rizal province and a classic family and barkada outing from Metro Manila, with picnic cottages and simple food
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; dry season (March-May) for clearer water
visible.commute_access: From Metro Manila, take a jeep or van to Tanay town (around 1.5–2 hours), then a tricycle to Daranak Falls (about 10 minutes).
visible.budget_note: Low entrance fee; cottages extra.

visible.name: Diniwid Beach
visible.address: Barangay Balabag, Boracay Island, Malay, Aklan
visible.description: Boracay ganda, minus the crowd! Diniwid Beach is a small cove just north of White Beach Station 1, reached by a footpath that winds around the rocky headland. The sand is the same fine white and the water just as clear, but with a fraction of the people. A few chill bars and boutique resorts line the shore, the swimmin
visible.best_time_to_visit: Afternoon to sunset, dry season
visible.commute_access: Walk the rock path from the north end of Station 1, or take a short e-trike ride.
visible.budget_note: Free beach.

visible.address: Butanding Visitor Center, Brgy. Dancalan, Donsol, Sorsogon
visible.description: Swim next to the biggest fish in the world – a true bucket-list moment! Donsol in Sorsogon is famous for its butanding, gentle whale sharks that feed in the bay during the season. Register at the Visitor Center in Dancalan, watch the short briefing, then head out on a boat with a trained Butanding Interaction Officer (
visible.best_time_to_visit: February to May peak; season roughly November to June
visible.visit_duration: Half day (3-4 hours on the boat)

visible.budget_note: Registration fee per person plus boat rental shared by up to around 6 people; snorkel gear rental extra.

visible.name: Eden Nature Park
visible.address: Toril District, Davao City
visible.description: Pine trees, cool mountain air and a sky ride over the forest - Eden Nature Park is Davao's favourite escape from the city heat. Set on 75 hectares in the hills of Toril, it mixes gardens and trails with adventure rides like the Skyrider, Skycycle and the 95-foot Skyswing. Take the 45-minute guided shuttle tour to see t
visible.best_time_to_visit: Morning to early afternoon (open daily, 9am-5pm for day guests)
visible.commute_access: About 1-1.5 hours by car from downtown Davao via Toril; the park runs shuttles from the city on some schedules.
visible.budget_note: Day tour packages with lunch available; rides extra.

visible.name: El Nido Island Hopping Tour A (Big Lagoon, Small Lagoon, Secret Lagoon)
visible.address: Bacuit Bay, Miniloc Island, El Nido, Palawan
visible.description: Ito ang tour na pinaka-iconic sa El Nido! Tour A takes your bangka through Bacuit Bay's towering limestone karsts to the famous lagoons of Miniloc Island: paddle a kayak into the emerald Big Lagoon, swim or kayak through the narrow gap of Small Lagoon, and squeeze through a hole in the rock into the tiny Secret Lagoon.
visible.best_time_to_visit: November to May (dry season); early morning start
visible.commute_access: Fly to El Nido (Lio) Airport or Puerto Princesa then van about 5-6 hours to El Nido town; tours depart from El Nido town beach with hotel pickup.
visible.budget_note: Shared tour around PHP 1,200-1,800 with lunch, plus the El Nido eco-tourism fee and kayak rental.

visible.name: El Nido Island Hopping Tour C (Hidden Beach, Secret Beach, Matinloc Shrine)

visible.commute_access: From Baguio's Dangwa/Slaughterhouse area, take a Halsema-bound bus or van toward Atok/Sagada and alight at Sayangan, Paoay (about 2 hours), or join a Baguio–Ato
visible.budget_note: Entrance fee applies (around ₱100–₱150).

visible.name: Ogtong Cave
visible.address: Ogtong Cave Resort, Barangay Pooc, Santa Fe, Bantayan Island, Cebu
visible.description: Pampalamig sa tanghaling tapat! Ogtong Cave is a cave pool of cool, crystal-clear water inside a beachfront resort just north of Santa Fe. Climb down the steps and take a dip under the limestone ceiling, a perfect break from the Bantayan heat. Your entrance also lets you use the resort's beach and pool, so it's easy to
visible.best_time_to_visit: Midday, to cool off
visible.commute_access: About 5-10 minutes by tricycle from Santa Fe port.
visible.budget_note: Entrance around PHP 100-120.

visible.name: Once Islas
visible.address: Once Islas (Eleven Islands), Zamboanga City
visible.description: Eleven islands, few crowds and powdery sandbars - Once Islas is Zamboanga's quieter island adventure. Opened to tourism in July 2018, the group is managed with the Banguingui community, and four of its islands welcome visitors: Bisaya-Bisaya, Baung-Baung, Buh-Buh and Sirommon. Expect white sand, sandbars, clear water f
visible.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, calm mornings
visible.commute_access: Book through the Zamboanga City tourism office; land transfer to the jump-off then boat to the islands.
visible.budget_note: Packaged tours via the tourism office.

visible.name: Osmeña Peak
visible.address: Barangay Mantalongon, Dalaguete, Cebu
visible.description: Summit na pang-beginner, view na pang-pro! Osmeña Peak in Mantalongon, Dalaguete is often called Cebu's highest peak, yet the hike from the jump-off takes only around 20-30 minutes. At the top, you get a wild landscape of jagged, pointed grassy hills that people compare to the Chocolate Hills, with the sea on both side
visible.best_time_to_visit: Sunrise, in the dry season
visible.visit_duration: 2-3 hours (whole day with the Kawasan traverse)
visible.commute_access: Bus to Dalaguete town (about 2.5-3 hours from Cebu South Bus Terminal), then habal-habal up to Mantalongon jump-off (about 30-45 minutes).
visible.budget_note: Small environmental fee plus habal-habal; guides optional.

visible.name: Pagsanjan Falls (Cavinti Falls) Boat Ride
visible.address: Bumbungan River, Pagsanjan / Cavinti, Laguna
visible.description: The OG Pinoy adventure: shooting the rapids! Two skilled bangkeros paddle and push your narrow canoe upstream through a deep, jungle-covered gorge, past rock walls and over boulder-strewn rapids, until you reach the thundering falls. Officially it is Cavinti Falls, since it sits in neighboring Cavinti, but everyone sti
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekdays; cooler months for a comfortable ride
visible.commute_access: From Manila, take a bus to Santa Cruz, Laguna (around 2.5–3 hours from Buendia, Cubao or Alabang), then a jeep to Pagsanjan town and a tricycle to an accredited
visible.budget_note: Boat rides are priced per person or per boat via the town's accredited stations; book only through official counters to avoid touts.

visible.name: Palaui Island and Cape Engaño Lighthouse
visible.address: Palaui Island, Barangay San Vicente, Santa Ana, Cagayan
visible.description: Palaui is the wild northeastern tip of Luzon: a protected island with empty beaches, clear coves and a Spanish-era lighthouse on a grassy cliff. Boats leave Port San Vicente in Santa Ana. Most trips land at Engaño Cove, where a steep 15 to 20 minute hike leads to the 1892 Cape Engaño Lighthouse and a 360-degree view of
visible.best_time_to_visit: March to June for calmer seas; avoid amihan (November–February) swells
visible.commute_access: Fly or bus to Tuguegarao, then travel to Santa Ana, Cagayan, and take a chartered boat from San Vicente Port. Boats need coast guard clearance before leaving.
visible.budget_note: Boat hire at Port San Vicente runs ₱900 to ₱4,950 per boat depending on the itinerary, split across your group. Santa Ana also collects a ₱20 environmental fee from non-residents at the town boundary. Visitors register at Engaño Cove and go with an accredited guide.

visible.name: Paliton Beach
visible.address: Barangay Paliton, San Juan, Siquijor
visible.description: Sunset spot ng Siquijor! Paliton Beach in San Juan is a small, powdery white-sand beach framed by leaning coconut palms, and it's the image you'll see on many Siquijor postcards. There are no big resorts, just locals, a few backpackers and a palm-lined road that's a photo spot in itself. Swim in the calm, shallow water
visible.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon to sunset
visible.commute_access: About 30-40 minutes by scooter or tricycle from Siquijor port, near San Juan town.
visible.budget_note: Free.

visible.name: Paoay Church (St. Augustine Church)
visible.address: Marcos Avenue, Paoay, Ilocos Norte
visible.description: Massive buttresses, golden coral stone and UNESCO status - Paoay Church is the Ilocos icon you have seen on every postcard. Built from 1694 to 1710 by Augustinian friars, the Church of St. Augustine is the best-known example of 'Earthquake Baroque': 24 huge buttresses, each about 1.67 meters thick, brace its walls agai
visible.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon to early evening; Nov-Apr dry season
visible.commute_access: Fly Manila–Laoag (about 1 hour) or take a Partas/Fariñas/Maria de Leon bus to Laoag (around 9–11 hours). From Laoag, ride a jeep or van to Paoay (about 30 minut
visible.budget_note: Free; respect mass schedules.

visible.name: Patar Beach
visible.address: Barangay Patar, Bolinao, Pangasinan
visible.description: Patar is Bolinao's long, golden-sand beach and the base for most Pangasinan beach trips. The sand is soft, the water is usually calm, and the sunsets over the West Philippine Sea are the main event. Rent a cottage, swim, then walk to the rock formations at the far end of the beach for photos. Nearby you can stack your
visible.best_time_to_visit: March to May and dry months; arrive by 5 PM for sunset
visible.commute_access: Direct buses from Cubao or Pasay to Bolinao (Five Star, Dagupan Bus, Victory Liner; about 6 hours, around ₱459), then a tricycle to Patar.
visible.budget_note: Entrance is ₱30–₱50 per person depending on the season, plus Bolinao's ₱40 environmental fee (valid three days for all town spots). Cottages are ₱500–₱1,000. A tricycle day tour of Bolinao is about ₱1,500 for up to four people.

visible.name: People's Park in the Sky
visible.address: Mt. Sungay, Dapdap East, Tagaytay City, Cavite
visible.description: The top of Tagaytay, with a Marcos-era story to match. People's Park in the Sky sits on Mt. Sungay, the highest point of Cavite, where the 'Palace in the Sky' mansion was rushed for a planned visit by US President Ronald Reagan that never happened. Today the unfinished concrete shell is a public park. Climb up past the
visible.best_time_to_visit: Clear mornings; dry season (December-May)
visible.commute_access: From Olivarez Plaza, take a jeep bound for People's Park/Calamba to the base (around 20 minutes), then a short uphill walk or shuttle.
visible.budget_note: Small entrance fee.

visible.name: Pescador Island
visible.address: Off Panagsama, Moalboal, Cebu
visible.description: Maliit na isla, malaking show sa ilalim! Pescador Island sits about 3 km off Moalboal, and it's the most common dive trip in town. A reef wraps around the whole island, shallow near shore and then dropping off to more than 40 meters, so snorkelers float over corals while divers go deep along the walls. Expect turtles,
visible.best_time_to_visit: Calm mornings in the dry season
visible.commute_access: Boat from Panagsama Beach, about 20-30 minutes.
visible.budget_note: Moalboal island-hopping boats are often shared or rented per boat; marine sanctuary fees apply.

visible.name: Philippine Eagle Center
visible.address: Malagos, Baguio District (Calinan area), Davao City
visible.description: Come face to face with the national bird - one of the biggest and rarest eagles on Earth. The Philippine Eagle Center in Malagos, run by the Philippine Eagle Foundation, keeps around 30 Philippine eagles plus other raptors in a forested setting at the edge of Davao City. Seeing that shaggy crest and huge wingspan up cl
visible.best_time_to_visit: Morning, when the birds are active (open 8am-5pm)
visible.commute_access: About 1 hour by car or Grab from downtown Davao or Davao International Airport; jeepneys to Calinan then tricycle.
visible.budget_note: Entrance around PHP 150.

visible.name: Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary (Corella)
visible.address: Philippine Tarsier Foundation, Barangay Canapnapan, Corella, Bohol
visible.description: Meet the tiny primate with the giant eyes! The Philippine Tarsier Foundation's sanctuary in Corella keeps tarsiers in natural forest, where guides point them out clinging to branches. Tarsiers are among the world's smallest primates, about the size of an adult fist, and their huge eyes are fixed in their skulls, so the
visible.best_time_to_visit: Morning
visible.commute_access: About 30 minutes by car from Tagbilaran; on most countryside tours.
visible.budget_note: Small entrance fee.

visible.name: Picnic Grove
visible.address: Tagaytay–Calamba Road, Sungay East, Tagaytay City, Cavite
visible.description: Baon, banig at Taal view - Picnic Grove is the classic Tagaytay family day out. Spread across the gentle slopes of Tagaytay Ridge, this big park has been a go-to for generations, with rentable huts and tables facing Taal Lake and Taal Volcano. When you are done eating, ride the zipline or cable car across the slope, go
visible.best_time_to_visit: Clear weekday mornings; Dec-Feb for the coolest weather
visible.commute_access: Take a Tagaytay-bound bus to Olivarez Plaza, then a jeep toward Calamba/Talisay and alight at Picnic Grove (around 15 minutes).
visible.budget_note: Low entrance fee; huts, zipline and horses priced separately.

visible.name: Pintô Art Museum
visible.address: 1 Sierra Madre Street, Grand Heights, San Roque, Antipolo City, Rizal
visible.description: White Mediterranean-style buildings, lush gardens and walls full of Filipino art - Pinto Art Museum is Antipolo's most Instagrammable culture trip. Opened as a museum in 2010 by neurologist and collector Dr. Joven Cuanang, it spreads across six buildings on about 12,000 square meters in Grand Heights, designed in an or
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings for fewer crowds and softer light
visible.commute_access: From Cubao or Shaw, take an Antipolo-bound jeep/UV Express to Antipolo, then a tricycle to Grand Heights (around 1–1.5 hours total). Grab/taxi from Metro Manila
visible.budget_note: Entrance fee applies with student/senior discounts.

visible.name: Plaza Salcedo and Vigan Dancing Fountain
visible.address: Plaza Salcedo, Vigan City, Ilocos Sur
visible.description: Pagdilim sa Vigan, tara sa Plaza Salcedo! Vigan's main plaza, named after the conquistador Juan de Salcedo, stretches beside the earthquake-baroque St. Paul Metropolitan Cathedral and the Provincial Capitol. At night, its long pool turns into the Vigan Dancing Fountain, a free show of water, lights and music that local
visible.best_time_to_visit: Evening for the fountain show; Nov-Apr dry season
visible.commute_access: Walkable from Calle Crisologo (about 5 minutes).
visible.budget_note: Free.

visible.name: Poblacion Makati (Bar District)
visible.address: Poblacion, Makati, Metro Manila
visible.description: Makati's old town by day, the city's favorite bar crawl by night! Poblacion is where Makati began, and its narrow streets and old houses now hold speakeasies, rooftop bars, craft cocktail spots and cheap-beer hangouts, all walkable from each other. Start with dinner, then hop from a chill bar to a louder one as the nig
visible.best_time_to_visit: Thursday to Saturday nights, from around 8 PM
visible.commute_access: Ride-hailing or taxi is easiest; Guadalupe MRT-3 station and Kalayaan Avenue jeepneys are nearby, then walk the inner streets.
visible.budget_note: Spend depends on how many bars you hit; casual bars are cheap while cocktail bars and rooftops cost more per drink. Many bars are free to enter on weeknights.

visible.name: Port Barton Island Hopping
visible.address: Port Barton, Barangay Poblacion, San Vicente, Palawan
visible.description: Slow life sa isang fishing village sa Palawan! Port Barton, a barangay of San Vicente between Puerto Princesa and El Nido, is loved for its laid-back pace and fewer boats than El Nido. visible.best_time_to_visit: December to May
visible.commute_access: About 3-4 hours by van from Puerto Princesa, or around 4 hours from El Nido.
visible.budget_note: Shared tours around PHP 1,000-1,500 with lunch, plus a small environmental fee (around PHP 50).

visible.name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park (Underground River)
visible.address: Sabang, Barangay Cabayugan, Puerto Princesa City, Palawan
visible.description: Paddle into a river that flows under a mountain! The Puerto Princesa Underground River is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New 7 Wonders of Nature, and it lives up to the hype. visible.best_time_to_visit: November to May dry season; weekday mornings
visible.commute_access: From Puerto Princesa airport, van about 2 hours to Sabang wharf, then boat about 15-20 minutes.
visible.budget_note: Day tours with transport, permit and lunch usually around PHP 1,800-2,500.

visible.name: Puka Shell Beach
visible.address: Barangay Yapak, Boracay Island, Malay, Aklan
visible.description: Ang chill side ng Boracay! Puka Shell Beach sits on the island's northern shore, a short tricycle ride from White Beach, and feels a world away from the Station 2 crowds. The sand is coarser, made of crushed shells, and the water is a deep turquoise with livelier waves. There are just a couple of restaurants and vendor
visible.best_time_to_visit: Morning to mid-afternoon, dry season
visible.commute_access: About 15-20 minutes by e-trike from White Beach Station 1.
visible.budget_note: Free beach; bring cash for food and e-trike.

visible.name: Rizal Park / Luneta Park
visible.address: Roxas Boulevard, Ermita, Manila
visible.description: The heart of the nation, and still the classic free family gala. Rizal Park, or Luneta, covers 58 hectares by Manila Bay, where Jose Rizal was executed on December 30, 1896, and where Philippine independence was proclaimed in 1946. visible.best_time_to_visit: Early morning or late afternoon into evening
visible.commute_access: Very accessible by LRT-1 United Nations, buses, jeepneys, taxis, and ride-hailing along Taft, Kalaw, and Roxas Boulevard.
visible.budget_note: No required entrance spend is listed for the basic visit. Transport, parking, food, rentals, special attractions, and optional activities may still cost extra.

visible.name: Sabang Beach Baler (Surfing)
visible.address: Sabang, Baler, Aurora

visible.best_time_to_visit: October to February for bigger surf; summer for gentler beginner waves
visible.commute_access: From Manila (Cubao/Sampaloc), take a Genesis/Joy Bus or Aurora-bound bus to Baler (around 5–7 hours via Nueva Ecija), then a tricycle to Sabang.
visible.budget_note: Surf lessons with board usually priced per hour.

visible.name: Sabtang Island and Chavayan Village

visible.best_time_to_visit: March to May for calmer seas; take the first boat between 6 and 7 AM

visible.name: Sagada Lemon Pie House
visible.address: Sagada South Road, Ambasing, Sagada, Mountain Province

visible.commute_access: Short walk south of the town center along the main road toward Ambasing.

visible.name: Salagdoong Beach

visible.commute_access: About 30-45 minutes by scooter or tricycle from Siquijor or Larena port.
visible.budget_note: Small entrance and parking fees.

visible.name: Sambawan Island

visible.description: Biliran's answer to paradise! Sambawan is made up of two main islands with grassy hills, white sand and super clear water. Trek up the hill for the best view of the island, with the thin beach strip below and Maripipi Island across the water, then snorkel or dive right off the shore since a dive camp operates on the is

visible.commute_access: Ride a van from Tacloban or Ormoc to Naval, Biliran (about 2 hours). Take a ferry from Naval to Maripipi, then a small boat to Sambawan (about 20 minutes). Grou
visible.budget_note: Costs cover the ferry from Naval to Maripipi, a hired boat to Sambawan, and the entrance and environmental fees collected on the island. Overnight cottages and tent spots are paid separately.

visible.name: San Agustin Church
visible.address: General Luna Street, Intramuros, Manila
visible.description: Over 400 years old and still standing - San Agustin Church is the oldest stone church in the Philippines and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Saud Beach in Pagudpud, at the very top of Luzon, is a long curve of fine white sand fringed by coconut palms, with clear emerald water and the Bangui windmills on the horizon. Resorts line the shore, yet it still feels wide and calm compared to busier beaches down south. Swim

visible.commute_access: From Laoag, take a bus or van bound for Pagudpud/Aparri (about 1.5–2 hours), then a tricycle to Saud. Direct buses from Manila also reach Pagudpud (around 11–13
visible.budget_note: Public beach access is cheap (small entrance/environmental fees); resorts charge for cottages and day use.

visible.name: Session Road
visible.address: Session Road, Baguio City
visible.description: Ang main street ng Baguio, at ang pinaka-masarap lakarin. Session Road runs 1.7 km uphill through the heart of downtown, from the Burnham Park side up toward SM Baguio, with the steps to Baguio Cathedral along the way. Both sides are packed with old-school bakeshops, cafés, restaurants, bookshops and souvenir stores, s
visible.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon to evening; Sundays for the car-free walk; February for Panagbenga
visible.commute_access: Walking distance from most downtown hotels and the Gov. Pack Road bus terminals.
visible.budget_note: Free to walk; meals and coffee from around ₱150–₱600.

visible.name: Siargao Island Hopping (Naked, Daku, Guyam Islands)
visible.address: Off General Luna, Siargao, Surigao del Norte
visible.description: Three islands, one perfect Siargao day! This classic half-day hop from General Luna starts at Naked Island (Pansukian), a bare strip of white sand with zero trees, just you, the sand and the blue. visible.best_time_to_visit: Early morning; March to October for calmer seas
visible.commute_access: Boats depart from General Luna's boulevard/port area; many resorts arrange pickup.
visible.budget_note: Shared tours around PHP 1,000-1,500 with lunch; island entrance fees small. Private boats per group.

visible.name: Simala Shrine (Monastery of the Holy Eucharist)
visible.address: Barangay Lindogon, Simala, Sibonga, Cebu
visible.description: Parang castle sa burol! Simala Shrine, officially the Monastery of the Holy Eucharist in Lindogon, Sibonga, is one of Cebu's biggest Marian pilgrimage sites, famous for its fairy-tale towers and the image of Our Lady of Lindogon, which devotees say was seen weeping. Inside, halls display letters and objects from people
visible.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; avoid Sundays and holidays for fewer crowds
visible.commute_access: Bus from Cebu South Bus Terminal to Sibonga (about 1.5-2 hours), then habal-habal or jeep to Simala.
visible.budget_note: Free entry; donations and candle offerings optional.

visible.name: Sirao Flower Garden
visible.address: Barangay Sirao, Cebu City, Cebu
visible.description: Cebu's 'Little Amsterdam' up in the mountains. Sirao Flower Garden is a hillside farm of bright celosia blooms in reds, oranges and yellows, dotted with windmills, a giant hand sculpture and other photo installations. Wear something bright and you will blend right into the flower rows. The cool mountain air makes it a
visible.best_time_to_visit: Early weekday mornings
visible.commute_access: About 45 minutes to 1 hour by car or habal-habal from Cebu City via the Busay–Sirao road.
visible.budget_note: Small entrance fee.

visible.name: Sky Ranch Tagaytay
visible.address: Tagaytay–Nasugbu Road, Kaybagal South, Tagaytay City, Cavite
visible.description: Ferris wheel with a Taal view? Sky Ranch na! Opened in 2013 on the Tagaytay ridge, this SM-run amusement park is famous for the Sky Eye, a 63-meter Ferris wheel with sweeping views of Taal Lake and Taal Volcano. Add family rides, carnival games and snack stalls and you have an easy, nostalgic barkada or family afternoo
visible.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon into early evening; weekdays to avoid lines
visible.commute_access: From Manila, take a Tagaytay/Nasugbu-bound bus from PITX, Buendia or Coastal Mall (around 1.5–2.5 hours) and alight at Sky Ranch/Olivarez area. Jeeps run along
visible.budget_note: Entrance plus per-ride tickets or ride-all passes.

visible.name: Sogod Bay Diving and Whale Sharks (Padre Burgos)
visible.address: Padre Burgos, Southern Leyte
visible.description: Underwater dream trip! Padre Burgos is the diving town of Sogod Bay, which the Department of Tourism says hosts over 20 marine protected areas and about 350 coral species. Dive the famed Napantao site and the walls around Limasawa Island, or go on a night dive to hunt for macro life like nudibranchs, frogfish, pipefish
visible.best_time_to_visit: November to May for whale shark season and calmer water
visible.commute_access: Fly to Tacloban and drive about 3 hours south, or take a ferry from Cebu to Maasin, then a short ride to Padre Burgos.
visible.budget_note: Sogod Bay Scuba Resort's 2026 rates: snorkeling day trip ₱1,000 including boat and marine park fees; guided dives ₱2,350 per dive with your own gear or ₱2,500 with rental gear; marine park fees ₱150-200 per dive; whale shark snorkel tour ₱4,000 per person (minimum 6).

visible.name: Sohoton Caves and Natural Bridge Park
visible.address: Barangay Guirang, Basey, Samar
visible.description: Ang hidden adventure ng Samar! Sohoton Caves and Natural Bridge Park in Basey covers 841 hectares of caves, underground rivers, waterfalls and thick forest, protected since 1935. The highlight is a natural stone bridge linking two mountains, rising about 120 meters high. Trips start with a boat ride upriver from Basey,
